text: Chapter 3. Insurance and Indemnification F. Workers' Compensation Insurance 1. [3:515] Workers' Compensation Benefits—In General: Workers' compensation insurance is designed to cover the insured employer's liability under the California Workers' Compensation Act (Labor Code § 3200 et seq.). The Act provides a comprehensive system of remedies administered by the Workers' Compensation Appeals Board (WCAB): • Under the statutory scheme, an employee injured in the workplace is entitled to workers' compensation benefits if the following “conditions of compensation” exist at the time of injury: — both the employer and employee are subject to provisions of Workers' Compensation Act; — the employee is performing service related to and within the course and scope of employment; — the injury is proximately caused by employment; and — the employee's injury is not intentionally self-inflicted, does not arise out of an altercation in which the injured employee is the initial physical aggressor, is not caused by the employee's commission of certain felonies or intoxication, and does not arise out of voluntary off-duty recreational activities.
